method: Direct urllib GET plus official page content retrieval for eCFR pages. No account or login was used.

sources.title: UPS File a Claim
sources.check: Direct HTTP 200 and official UPS page content; page states 60 days after scheduled delivery and lists evidence to retain.

sources.title: UPS Supporting Documents for Claims
sources.check: Direct HTTP 200 and official UPS page content; invoice/value evidence and damage photos are listed.

sources.title: FedEx File a Claim
sources.check: Direct HTTP 200 and official FedEx page content; current page states 60 days domestic damage/missing contents, 21 days international, and nine months for lost shipments, each from ship date.

sources.title: USPS Domestic Claims — The Basics
sources.check: Direct HTTP 200 and official USPS page content; damage/missing contents no later than 60 days from mailing and lost windows vary by service.

sources.title: USPS Domestic Mail Manual 609
sources.check: Direct HTTP 200 and Postal Explorer official manual content; service-specific lost-article filing windows are listed.

sources.title: 49 U.S.C. § 14706 (GPO 2024 edition)
sources.check: Direct HTTP 200 and U.S. Government Publishing Office text; § (e) states the minimum nine-month claim filing period.

sources.title: 49 CFR § 370.3
sources.check: Official eCFR section content retrieved; rule describes written claim particulars. Direct urllib probe reaches federalregister.gov anti-bot interstitial in this environment.

sources.title: 49 CFR § 370.5
sources.check: Official eCFR section content retrieved; acknowledgment within 30 days is stated. Direct urllib probe reaches federalregister.gov anti-bot interstitial in this environment.

sources.title: 49 CFR § 370.9
sources.check: Official eCFR section content retrieved; disposition within 120 days and written status updates each succeeding 60-day period are stated. Direct urllib probe reaches federalregister.gov anti-bot interstitial in this environment.

superseded_link.finding: OLRC website returned its maintenance page during verification; references now point to the official GPO 2024 U.S. Code section, which returned HTTP 200 and contains § 14706.
